title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
act: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

source.version_note: Official India Code text includes the commencement notification dated 13 November 2025.

legal_context.subject: Protection and processing of digital personal data
legal_context.purpose: The Act provides for processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognises an individual's right to protect personal data while allowing lawful processing.
legal_context.important_note: The Act has phased commencement under the notification dated 13 November 2025. The AI must check the applicable commencement date of a provision before representing that provision as currently operative.

key_definitions.personal_data: Data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data.
key_definitions.data_principal: The individual to whom the personal data relates, with specified rules for children and persons with disability.
key_definitions.data_fiduciary: A person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
key_definitions.data_processor: A person who processes personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary.
key_definitions.consent_manager: A person registered with the Board who enables a Data Principal to give, manage, review and withdraw consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform.
key_definitions.child: An individual who has not completed eighteen years of age.

core_principles.lawful_processing: Personal data processing must be carried out in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Act and for lawful purposes.
core_principles.consent: The Act provides a framework for processing personal data based on consent and certain legitimate uses.
core_principles.notice: The Act contains requirements concerning notice to the Data Principal in specified circumstances.
core_principles.purpose_and_scope: The framework regulates processing of digital personal data and establishes responsibilities for Data Fiduciaries and rights and duties of Data Principals.

rights: Right to access information about personal data and its processing, subject to the Act.
Right to correction and erasure of personal data, subject to applicable conditions.
Right to nominate another individual to exercise rights in accordance with the Act.
data_principal_rights.important_note: The availability and exercise of each right is subject to the applicable provisions, conditions and commencement status under the Act.

duties: Comply with applicable law while exercising rights under the Act.
Provide information that is authentic where required.
Not impersonate another person in specified interactions.
Not suppress material information while obtaining specified documents or services.
Provide information that is not false or misleading in specified circumstances.

key_obligations: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective compliance with the Act.
Take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches.
Provide required information and respond to Data Principal requests in accordance with the Act.
Erase personal data when retention is no longer necessary for the specified purpose, subject to applicable legal requirements.
Appoint or designate required personnel where applicable.
data_fiduciary_obligations.security_principle: A Data Fiduciary must protect personal data through reasonable security safeguards appropriate to the Act and applicable requirements.

special_protection: The Act contains special provisions concerning processing of children's personal data.
Verifiable parental consent requirements apply under the relevant provisions.
The Act restricts certain processing practices involving children, subject to the statutory framework.

data_breach.principle: The Act contains obligations concerning personal data breaches, including requirements to notify the Data Protection Board of India and affected Data Principals in circumstances specified by the Act.

data_protection_board.name: Data Protection Board of India
role: Exercise powers and perform functions assigned under the Act.
Deal with breaches and contraventions within its statutory jurisdiction.
Perform functions connected with enforcement of the Act.
data_protection_board.establishment_note: The Data Protection Board of India was established by notification dated 13 November 2025.

commencement.important_note: Different provisions of the Act commence on different dates under the Central Government notification.
commencement.rag_rule: The RAG system must use the applicable commencement date when answering questions about whether a particular DPDP Act provision is currently operative.

application_to_alimony_plus.sensitive_data_rule: Alimony Plus should minimise collection and retention of personal information and should process only information necessary for the intended service.
application_to_alimony_plus.security_rule: Sensitive case information and uploaded documents should be protected using appropriate technical and organisational safeguards.
application_to_alimony_plus.privacy_rule: The application should avoid unnecessarily exposing personal legal information and should implement appropriate access controls, audit mechanisms and data-handling safeguards.
application_to_alimony_plus.commencement_rule: The system must not present a DPDP Act obligation as currently enforceable without checking the commencement status of the relevant provision.

rag_use: Answer high-level questions about digital personal-data protection.
Explain Data Principal, Data Fiduciary and related terminology.
Support privacy and security design decisions for Alimony Plus.
Explain relevant user rights when the applicable provisions are in force.
Identify privacy-related risks involving uploaded documents and case information.
Retrieve the applicable commencement status of DPDP Act provisions.
Provide citation-backed explanations rather than presenting the Act as blanket legal advice.
safety_rule: The AI must not claim that Alimony Plus is legally compliant merely because it follows selected provisions. Compliance requires assessment of the complete applicable legal and technical framework.
human_review: Questions concerning legal compliance, regulatory obligations, data-sharing arrangements, breach response or interpretation of the Act should be reviewed by an appropriate privacy/legal professional.
